.

SplitScore(
C_{0},m
) in (
3
) can be written as

\begin{split}&\left(\sum_{i\in N_{0}}\widehat{r}_{i}^{2}\right)-\sum_{l=1}^{2}\sum_{i\in N_{l}(\widehat{a})}(\widehat{r}_{i}-\frac{1}{1\vee\texttt{\#}N_{l}(\widehat{a})}\sum_{i\in N_{l}(\widehat{a})}\widehat{r}_{i})^{2}\\
&=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat{r}_{i}^{2}\right)-\sum_{l=1}^{2}\sum_{i\in\{t:\boldsymbol{X}_{t}\in C_{l}\}}(\widehat{r}_{i}-\frac{1}{1\vee\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}\}}\sum_{i\in\{t:\boldsymbol{X}_{t}\in C_{l}\}}\widehat{r}_{i})^{2}\\
&=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat{r}_{i}^{2}\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{l=1}^{2}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}}(\widehat{r}_{i}-\frac{1}{1\vee\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}\}}\sum_{i\in\{t:\boldsymbol{X}_{t}\in C_{l}\}}\widehat{r}_{i})^{2}\\
&=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat{r}_{i}^{2}\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left[\sum_{l=1}^{2}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}}\left(\widehat{r}_{i}-\frac{1}{1\vee\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}\}}\sum_{i\in\{t:\boldsymbol{X}_{t}\in C_{l}\}}\widehat{r}_{i}\right)\right]^{2}\\
&=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat{r}_{i}^{2}\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\widehat{r}_{i}-\sum_{l=1}^{2}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}}\frac{\sum_{i\in\{t:\boldsymbol{X}_{t}\in C_{l}\}}\widehat{r}_{i}}{1\vee\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l}\}}\right)^{2},\end{split}

(A.26)

where the third equality holds since

, and that the square of an indicator function equals the indicator function itself.

It is worth noting that we actually have
X_{\widehat{a}q}=0
, which is deduced from: 1) if

, the corresponding split score is zero, and 2) our assumption that all nodes are valid before the first
2K
updates. Thus,
\{C_{1,J},C_{2,J}\}=\{C_{1},C_{2}\}
with

. With this, and

at the
s

A.26
) has the same expression as in the curly brackets of (
A.4
) with
J=\{m\}
. We have finished the proof for the scenario with
0<s\leq K
.

. For the completeness of notation, we define
a_{0,\mathchoice{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern 2.0mu\textstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\textstyle\mkern for all vector

\mkern 2.0mu\textstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\textstyle\mkern 0.0mu\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraita}$}}}\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr

\hfil\textstyle c\hfil

and set
J
. Also, recall that summation over an empty set is defined to be zero.

By (
A.28
) and (
A.9
), on the event
E_{41}\cap E_{42}
defined in (
A.10
) with
t_{1}=t_{2}=\log{(n)}n^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{q_{1}}}
, it holds that for each
s\geq 0
and every set
J
with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
,

\begin{split}&|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\varepsilon_{i}(f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))|\\
&\leq t_{1}+t_{2}(M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\times 3\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1}+M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\iota_{s-1})\\
&=\log{(n)}n^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{q_{1}}}(3M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}p_{\min}^{-1}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}+M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\iota_{s-1}+1).\end{split}

(A.29)

Next, we proceed to establish an upper bound for the term
\sum_{i=1}^{n}(R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s,J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}
. First, when
s=0
, by the definitions of
R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})
and
\widehat{U}_{s,J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})
in (
A.3
),

\sum_{i=1}^{n}(R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s,J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}=0.

(A.30)

Meanwhile, when
s>0
, by (
A.3
) and the model assumption of
Y=f(\boldsymbol{X})+\varepsilon
, we deduce that

\begin{split}&\sum_{i=1}^{n}(R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s,J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}Y_{i}-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)^{2}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\right)\\
&\qquad+\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\right)-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})\\
&\qquad+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\varepsilon_{i}}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)^{2}.\end{split}

(A.31)

In addition, we have that for every measurable
q:\{0,1\}^{\texttt{\#}\mathcal{X}(J)}\mapsto\mathbb{R}
,

\begin{split}&\sum_{i=1}^{n}q(\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}\{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\times q(\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)\\
&=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}q_{l,J}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\boldsymbol{1}\{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)\\
&=0,\end{split}

(A.32)

where the second equality holds due to an interchange of the two outer summations and that
q_{l,J}=q(\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})
when
\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}
for each
l\in\mathcal{L}(J)
. Moreover, it holds that

\begin{split}&\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)^{2}\\
&=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\bigg(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\\
&\qquad-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})+\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\bigg)^{2}\\
&\leq\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\left(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})\right)^{2}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})\right)^{2},\end{split}

(A.33)

where the first inequality follows from that
\sum_{i=1}^{n}(b_{i}-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i})^{2}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i}^{2}
for all real
b_{i}
’s.

By (
A.31
)–(
A.33
) and Minkowski’s inequality, it holds that for each
s>0
and every set

with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2

\begin{split}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s,J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{n}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-\widehat{U}_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}+\left(\sum_{l=1}^{3}E_{l}\right)^{2},\end{split}

(A.34)

where

\begin{split}E_{1}&=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\right)-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})\right)^{2}},\\
E_{2}&=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\right)^{2}},\\
E_{3}&=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\varepsilon_{i}}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\right)^{2}}.\end{split}

We now establish bounds for
E_{1},E_{2},E_{3}
as follows. For
E_{1}
, note that

\begin{split}&\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\frac{\sum_{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}\right)-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})\\
&=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\left(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})}{\texttt{\#}\{i:\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}\}\vee 1}-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J})\right),\end{split}

(A.35)

where we rely on that
\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i\mathcal{X}(J)})=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}(J)}\boldsymbol{1}_{\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J}}\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})|\boldsymbol{X}_{i}\in C_{l,J})
almost surely for every set

(A.36)

By (

), it holds that on the event

, for each

\begin{split}\textnormal{RHS of \eqref{E1.1}}&\leq\frac{t_{4}n^{-1}\times M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\iota_{s-1}}{p_{\min}-\frac{t_{4}}{n}}+\frac{t_{4}n^{-1}\times 2\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}(p_{\min}-\frac{t_{4}}{n})}.\end{split}

(A.39)

Next, we proceed to deal with

(A.41)

,
(

&\leq(M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\times 3\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1}+M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\iota_{s-1})^{2}.\end{split}

(A.48)

By (
A.47
)–(
A.48
) and that
R_{0,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})=0
as defined in (
A.3
), it holds that on
E_{44}
, for each

and every set

with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
,

\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{(R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}-\mathbb{E}[(R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]\}\right|\leq t_{4}(3M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}p_{\min}^{-1}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}+M_{\mathcal{X}}^{2}\iota_{s-1})^{2}.

(A.49)

By (
A.45
), (
A.49
), the definition of
E_{46}
, and the choice of
t_{3}=t_{4}=t_{6}=\log{(n)}\sqrt{n}
, we conclude the desired result of (
A.15
).

B.1.4
Proof of (
A.20
)

Proof of (
A.20
):
At the
s
th round with
0<s\leq K
, let us consider
J=\{m\}
for any
m\in\{1,\cdots,M\}\backslash(\cup_{l=1}^{s-1}\widehat{J}_{l})
. We deduce that

\begin{split}&\left(\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}]\right)^{2}\\
&=\left\{\mathbb{E}\{f(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]+\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}\}\right\}^{2}\\
&=(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}-2g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})\times\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}\right\}\\
&\qquad+\left(\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}\}\right)^{2},\end{split}

(A.50)

where we recall that
g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})=\mathbb{E}\{f(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}\}
, which is defined in Section
3
.

Next, we proceed to deal with terms on the RHS of (
A.50
). By the assumption that
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
, Lemma
1
, the law of total expectation, Jensen’s inequality, and Lemma
6
, it holds that almost surely,

\begin{split}&\bigg|\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})\Big|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}\right\}\bigg|\\
&=\bigg|\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})\Big|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}\right\}\\
&\qquad-\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})\right\}\bigg|\\
&\leq\frac{\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}\mathbb{E}\left|\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})\right|\\
&\leq\frac{\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}(\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|+\mathbb{E}|R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|)\\
&\leq\frac{3\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]},\end{split}

(A.51)

where we rely on that
\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}]-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})
is a measurable function of
\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}
for
0<s\leq K
due to our assumption that
\widehat{J}_{l}\not=\widehat{J}_{k}
for each
1\leq l<k\leq 2K
.

By (
A.50
), (
A.51
), and that
\mathbb{E}[(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]=\textnormal{Var}(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))
by the definition of
g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})
, it holds that for each
0<s\leq K
and each
m\in\{1,\cdots,M\}\backslash(\cup_{l=1}^{s-1}\widehat{J}_{l})
,

\begin{split}&\left|\mathbb{E}[(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}))^{2}]-\textnormal{Var}(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))\right|\\
&\leq\frac{6\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}(\mathbb{E}|g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})|)+\frac{9\delta_{0}^{2}}{(p_{\min})^{2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]\\
&\leq\frac{21\delta_{0}}{(p_{\min})^{2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}],\end{split}

(A.52)

where we use the fact that
\delta_{0}\leq 1
and
p_{\min}\leq 1
, and the result due to Jensen’s inequality and the definition of
g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})
that

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}|g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})|&=\mathbb{E}\left|\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\right|\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}(\left|f(\boldsymbol{X})\right|+\left|\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})\right||\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\right]\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}\left|f(\boldsymbol{X})\right|+\mathbb{E}(\mathbb{E}(\left|f(\boldsymbol{X})\right||\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}))\\
&\leq 2\mathbb{E}\left|f(\boldsymbol{X})\right|\\
&\leq 2\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}.\end{split}

(A.53)

By (
A.52
), we have concluded the proof of (
A.20
).

B.1.5
Proof of (
A.24
)

Proof of (
A.24
):
For each
K<s\leq 2K
and every set
J
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
, let
\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)=\{l:\widehat{J}_{l}\subset J,1\leq l\leq K\}
,
\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)=\{l:\widehat{J}_{l}\cap J\not=\emptyset,K<l<s\}
, and
\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)=\{l:\widehat{J}_{l}\cap J=\emptyset,K<l<s\}
. Let us deduce that for each
K<s\leq 2K
and every
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
,

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}]\\
&=g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\\
&\qquad-\mathbb{E}\{\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\\
&\qquad-\mathbb{E}\{\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\\
&\qquad+\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(J)}]-\sum_{l\leq K,l\not\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\},\end{split}

(A.54)

where we use the definition of
g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})
in Section
3
, and the expression

R_{s}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})=\sum_{l=1}^{s}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]
, which follows from a recursive application of (
7
).

In light of (
A.54
), for each
s>K
and
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
, we define
F_{s}(J)
such that

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}]\\
&=F_{s}(J)+g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}].\end{split}

(A.55)

To deal with the third term on the RHS of (
A.55
), we deduce by the definition of
\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)
that for each
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
,

\begin{split}&\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\\
&=\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}g_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X})\right)+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}],\end{split}

(A.56)

and that almost surely

\begin{split}&\left|\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right|\\
&\leq 2\delta_{0}\times\frac{\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|+\mathbb{E}|R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq\frac{6\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}},\end{split}

(A.57)

where we use Lemma
6
, the result that
\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\}=0
for
l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)
, Jensen’s inequality, Lemma
1
,
the definition of
p_{\min}
in Condition
2
, and that
\texttt{\#}\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)\leq 2
due to the assumption that Algorithm
1
makes the initial
2K
updates with
\widehat{J}_{l}\not=\widehat{J}_{k}
for each
\{l,k\}\subset\{1,\cdots,2K\}
. In addition, with the required conditions for (
A.21
), Condition
3
, and the definition of
S_{1}^{*}
, we further have that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
,

\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}g_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X})=\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}),

(A.58)

where we note that
g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})=0
if
\textnormal{Var}(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
.

Under the required conditions for (
A.55
)–(
A.56
) and (
A.58
), we have that

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}\left(\left\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}]\right\}^{2}\right)-\mathbb{E}([g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})]^{2})\\
&=\mathbb{E}\bigg([F_{s}(J)]^{2}+\left[\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right]^{2}\\
&\qquad-2\left[\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right]\\
&\qquad\qquad\times\left[F_{s}(J)+g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})\right]\\
&\qquad+2[F_{s}(J)]\times[g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})]\bigg).\end{split}

(A.59)

Based on (
A.59
), our goal is to derive a result similar to (
A.52
) for the case with
K<s\leq 2K
by using the identity
\mathbb{E}\left([g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})]^{2}\right)=\textnormal{Var}\left(g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})\right)
, (
A.57
), and (
A.53
), along with some upper bound on
|F_{s}(J)|
. To this end, we obtain an upper bound for
|F_{s}(J)|
as follows.

Recall that
F_{s}(J)
is defined in (
A.55
), which is the sum of the last three terms on the RHS of (
A.54
). Let us establish an upper bound for each of these three terms, and begin with the term involving
\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)
. By the definition of
\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)
, Lemma
6
, Jensen’s inequality, Lemma
1
, it holds almost surely that for each
K<s\leq 2K
and each
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
,

\begin{split}&\left|\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\right|\\
&=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\Big|\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\\
&\qquad-\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right\}\Big|\\
&\leq\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\frac{3\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}\left|\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right|}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\frac{3\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\frac{9\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}([f(\boldsymbol{X})]^{2})}}{p_{\min}},\end{split}

(A.60)

where the first equality follows from Lemma
1
, law of total expectation, and the assumption that
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
.

Next, we now proceed to establish an upper bound for the last term on the RHS of (
A.54
). By Lemma
6
, Jensen’s inequality, and Lemma
1
, it holds almost surely that for each
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
,

\begin{split}&\Big|\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(J)}]-\sum_{l\leq K,l\not\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\Big|\\
&\leq\frac{3\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}\times\left[\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|+\mathbb{E}\left|\sum_{l\leq K,l\not\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right|\right]\\
&\leq\frac{3\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}\times\left[\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|+\mathbb{E}\left|R_{K}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})\right|+\mathbb{E}\left|\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]\right|\right]\\
&\leq\frac{3\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}\times\left[\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|+2\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}+2\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|+4\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\right]\\
&\leq\frac{27\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}},\end{split}

(A.61)

where the first inequality is due to an application of Lemma
6
, Jensen’s inequality, Lemma
1
, and the assumption that
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
; the second inequality follows from a recursive application of (
7
), the definition of
\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)
, and Jensen’s inequality; and that the third inequality is due to the definition of
\mathcal{L}_{1}(J)
, Lemma
1
, and the assumption that Algorithm
1
makes the initial
2K
updates with
\widehat{J}_{l}\not=\widehat{J}_{k}
for each
1\leq l<k\leq 2K
.

Next, the upper bound of the term
\mathbb{E}\{\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}
on the RHS of (
A.54
) is established as follows. By (
A.55
)–(
A.57
), and Lemma
4
along with the definition of
\mathcal{L}_{2}(J)
,

\begin{split}&\left|\mathbb{E}\{\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\right|\\
&=\left|\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\mathbb{E}\{F_{l}(\widehat{J}_{l})+g_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{q\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(\widehat{J}_{l})}\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{q-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{q})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\right|\\
&\leq\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\bar{F}_{l}(\widehat{J}_{l})\right)+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\left|\mathbb{E}\left[g_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X})-\Big(\sum_{q\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(\widehat{J}_{l})}g_{\widehat{J}_{q}}(\boldsymbol{X})\Big)\Big|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\right]\right|\\
&\qquad+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\left|\sum_{q\in\mathcal{L}_{1}(\widehat{J}_{l})}\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{q})}]-R_{q-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{q})}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}\}\right|\\
&\leq\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\bar{F}_{l}(\widehat{J}_{l})\right)+\texttt{\#}\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)\times\left(\frac{8\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}+\frac{6\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\right),\end{split}

(A.62)

where for each
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
and
K<l\leq 2K
,

\bar{F}_{l}(J)\coloneqq\inf\{c>0:|F_{l}(J)|\leq c\textnormal{ almost surely}\}.

By Lemma
4
, (
A.60
)–(
A.62
), the definition of
\bar{F}_{l}(J)
above, and that
F_{s}(J)
given in (
A.55
) is defined to be the sum of the last three terms on the RHS of (
A.54
), it holds that for each
K<s\leq K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}
,

\begin{split}\bar{F}_{s}(J)&\leq\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)}\bar{F}_{l}(\widehat{J}_{l})\right)+\texttt{\#}\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)\times\left(\frac{6\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}+\frac{8\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\right)\\
&\qquad+\left(\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)}\frac{9\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}([f(\boldsymbol{X})]^{2})}}{p_{\min}}\right)+\frac{27\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq\left(\sum_{l>K}^{s-1}\bar{F}_{l}(\widehat{J}_{l})\right)+(23(s-K-1)+27)\times\frac{\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq(23(\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{2}+27\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})\times\frac{\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq 50(\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{2}\times\frac{\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}},\end{split}

(A.63)

where the second inequality follows from Jensen’s inequality,
p_{\min}\leq 1
, and the fact that
\texttt{\#}\mathcal{L}_{2s}(J)\vee\texttt{\#}\mathcal{L}_{3s}(J)\leq s-K-1
. The third inequality stems from a recursive application of the second inequality. Recall that we have defined that
\sum_{l>K}^{K}1=0
.

By the identity
\mathbb{E}\left([g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})]^{2}\right)=\textnormal{Var}\left(g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\sum_{m\in J}g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X})\right)
, (
A.59
), (
A.63
), (
A.57
), and (
A.53
), it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
, for each
K<s\leq K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}
, each
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
,

\begin{split}&\left|\mathbb{E}[(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}))^{2}]-\textnormal{Var}\left[g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})-\left(\sum_{j\in J}g_{\{j\}}(\boldsymbol{X})\right)\right]\right|\\
&\leq\left(\frac{6\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\right)^{2}+\mathbb{E}[(F_{s}(J))^{2}]\\
&\qquad+\left(\frac{12\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\right)\times\left(\mathbb{E}\left|F_{s}(J)\right|+6\sqrt{\mathbb{E}([(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\right)\\
&\qquad+12\sqrt{\mathbb{E}([(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times\mathbb{E}|F_{s}(J)|\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]\left(\frac{36\delta_{0}^{2}}{p_{\min}^{2}}+\frac{2500\delta_{0}^{2}(\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{4}}{p_{\min}^{2}}+\frac{600\delta_{0}^{2}(\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{2}}{p_{\min}^{2}}+\frac{72\delta_{0}}{p_{\min}}+\frac{600\delta_{0}(\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{2}}{p_{\min}^{2}}\right)\\
&\leq 3808\delta_{0}{p_{\min}^{-2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}](\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{4},\end{split}

(A.64)

where we also use
p_{\min}\leq 1
and
\delta_{0}\leq 1
in the last inequality.

By (
A.64
), we have finished the proof of (
A.24
).

0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\displaystyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern 2.0mu\textstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\textstyle\mkern 0.0mu\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraita}$}}}\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\textstyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern 2.0mu\scriptstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mkern 0.0mu\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraita}$}}}\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\scriptstyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern 2.0mu\scriptscriptstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mkern 0.0mu\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraita}$}}}\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\scriptscriptstyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}_{2}),\end{split}

(A.67)

where the third equality is due to
\delta_{0}=0
. The results of (
A.66
)–(
A.67
) conclude the independence between
\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}
and
\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}
when
\texttt{\#}\mathcal{X}(m)=1
.

An application of above arguments to each feature group shows that feature groups
\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(1)},\cdots,\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(M)}
are independent when
\delta_{0}=0
. On the other hand, it is obvious that
\delta_{0}=0
if feature groups are independent. Therefore, we have finished the proof that
\delta_{0}=0
if and only if feature groups
\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(1)},\cdots,\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(M)}
are independent.

Now, we proceed to deal with the main assertion of Corollary
1
, and begin by clarifying notation usage: When
J=\{m\}
, we write that

h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})=h_{\{m\}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\{m)\}})=h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})
. Let us give an auxiliary result of (
A.68
) below, which is useful for our proof. By the assumption of independent features and the assumption on
h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})
’s, it holds that for each
m\in S_{1}
, each
J\in S_{2}
, every
H_{1}\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}(H_{1}\cap J)=1
, and every
H_{2}\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
m\not\in H_{2}
,

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(H_{1})})&=\mathbb{E}(h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(H_{1}\cap J)})\\
&=0,\\
\mathbb{E}(h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(H_{2})})&=\mathbb{E}(h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}))\\
&=0.\end{split}

(A.68)

Now, we show that, based on our assumption, for any nonrepeated sequence of sets
\widehat{J}_{l}
’s with
\texttt{\#}\widehat{J}_{l}=1
for
1\leq l\leq K
and
\texttt{\#}\widehat{J}_{l}=2
for
K<l\leq 2K
, it holds that for each
0<s\leq 2K
,

R_{s}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})=\sum_{l=1}^{s}h_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})})+\sum_{m\in(\cup_{k=K+1}^{s}\widehat{J}_{k})\backslash(\cup_{k=1}^{K}\widehat{J}_{k})}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}),

(A.69)

where we define that

h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})=0\textnormal{ if }J\not\in\{\{m\}:m\in S_{1}\}\cup S_{2},

(A.70)

and recall that summation over an empty set is defined to be zero, and that each set has distinct elements. It is important to note that (
A.69
) does not depend on the result of consistent feature selection.

Let us prove (
A.69
). Suppose it is true that

\begin{split}R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})&=\sum_{l=1}^{s-1}h_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})})+\sum_{m\in(\cup_{k=K+1}^{s-1}\widehat{J}_{k})\backslash(\cup_{k=1}^{K}\widehat{J}_{k})}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\end{split}

(A.71)

which in combination with (
A.68
) and the assumption that each element in the sequence
\{\widehat{J}_{l}\}
is unique leads to that

\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})})=\sum_{m\in\widehat{J}_{s}\cap(\cup_{l=1}^{s-1}\widehat{J}_{l})}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}).

(A.72)

In addition, by the assumption on
f(\boldsymbol{X})
and (
A.68
), it holds that

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})&=h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})+\sum_{m\in J}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}),\qquad\textnormal{ for each }J\textnormal{ with }\texttt{\#}J=2,\\
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})&=h_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}),\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\textnormal{ for each }J\textnormal{ with }\texttt{\#}J=1.\end{split}

(A.73)

By (
A.71
)–(
A.73
), the assumption that each element in the sequence
\{\widehat{J}_{l}\}
is unique, the definition that each set has distinct elements (and hence each element in
\cup J_{l}
is unique), and (
A.68
), it holds that for
\widehat{J}_{s}
with
\texttt{\#}\widehat{J}_{s}=2
,

\begin{split}R_{s}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})&=R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})})\\
&=R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})+\left(h_{\widehat{J}_{s}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})})+\sum_{m\in\widehat{J}_{s}}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\right)-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})})\\
&=\sum_{l=1}^{s-1}h_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})})+\sum_{m\in(\cup_{k=K+1}^{s-1}\widehat{J}_{k})\backslash(\cup_{k=1}^{K}\widehat{J}_{k})}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\\
&\qquad+\left(h_{\widehat{J}_{s}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})})+\sum_{m\in\widehat{J}_{s}}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\right)-\sum_{m\in\widehat{J}_{s}\cap(\cup_{l=1}^{s-1}\widehat{J}_{l})}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})\\
&=\sum_{l=1}^{s}h_{\widehat{J}_{l}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{l})})+\sum_{m\in(\cup_{k=K+1}^{s}\widehat{J}_{k})\backslash(\cup_{k=1}^{K}\widehat{J}_{k})}h_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)}),\end{split}

which concludes the desired result by induction in this scenario. The case with
\texttt{\#}\widehat{J}_{s}=1
can be proven similarly, and hence we omit the detail. We have finished the proof of the desired result (
A.69
).

)–(

2.0mu\textstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\textstyle\mkern 2.0mu\scriptscriptstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\scriptscriptstyle c\hfil$\crcr}}})|\leq M_{f}.

(A.79)

The results of (
A.78
)–(
A.79
) conclude the second assertion of Corollary
1
.

Lastly, we proceed to show the last assertion of Corollary
1
. The other regularity conditions are given as follows. Consider a modified Algorithm
1
such that
\widehat{J}_{l}\not=\widehat{J}_{k}
for each
\{l,k\}\subset\{1,\cdots,2K\}
. Assume that we are given an i.i.d. sample
(\boldsymbol{X}_{1},Y_{1}),\cdots,(\boldsymbol{X}_{n},Y_{n}),(\boldsymbol{X},Y)
satisfying Condition
1
. Assume that
p_{\min}\geq p_{01}\vee\frac{2\log{(n)}}{\sqrt{n}}
, and that
\iota_{-1}=\iota_{0}=0
. Assume
M\geq K\geq\texttt{\#}S_{1}^{*}\vee\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}
, , and that
M=O(n^{K_{01}})
for some arbitrary constant
K_{01}>0
.

Then, by Theorem
1
, it holds that
\mathbb{P}(\{S_{1}\not\subset\cup_{l=1}^{K}\widehat{J}_{l}\}\cup(S_{2}\not\subset\{\widehat{J}_{K+1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}}\}))=o(1)
. By this result and (
A.78
)–(
A.79
), we have finished the proof of Corollary
1
.

B.3
Proof of Theorem
2

Proof of Theorem
2
:
The sum of all sample split scores after the
(K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})
th round is given by

\begin{split}&n^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}(Y_{i}-\widehat{U}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}\right)-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(Y_{i}-\sum_{k=1}^{K}T_{k}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})\right)^{2}\\
&=\Delta+D_{2,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}+D_{1,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}+\widehat{\Gamma},\end{split}

(A.80)

where
\widehat{U}_{s}
’s are the sample predictive functions at the
s
th round defined in (
A.3
), and that

\begin{split}D_{1,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}&=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(Y_{i}-\widehat{U}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-R_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\varepsilon_{i}^{2},\\
D_{2,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}&=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})-R_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}_{i}))^{2}-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}.\end{split}

Here, we use the result
\mathbb{E}(R_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
from Lemma
1
and the assumption
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
to deduce that
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}=\textnormal{Var}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))=\Delta
.

We now establish the upper bounds for
|D_{2,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}|
and
|D_{1,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}|
by the results derived in the proof of Theorem
1
. By (
A.16
) of Theorem
1
, the definition (
A.3
) in Theorem
1
, and the assumed technical conditions, it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
defined in (
A.10
) of Theorem
1
,

\begin{split}|D_{2,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}|+|D_{1,K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}|\leq d_{n},\end{split}

(A.81)

where
d_{n}=L_{1}n^{-\frac{1}{2}}\log{(n)}(n^{\frac{1}{q_{1}}}\sqrt{2K}+\sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^{2K}\iota_{l-1}^{2}})(\iota_{2K-1}^{2}+\iota_{2K-1}+3)
, with technical parameters given in Theorem
1
.

The results of (
A.80
)–(
A.81
) are useful for analyzing our group feature importance measures. Consider
\textnormal{XMDI}_{ij}^{\dagger}
as an importance measure identical to
\textnormal{XMDI}_{ij}
, except that
\textnormal{XMDI}_{ij}^{\dagger}
calculates importance only up to the first
K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}
updates, with the remaining split scores ignored. That is,
\textnormal{XMDI}_{J}^{\dagger}=0
if
J\not\in\{\widehat{J}_{1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}\}
, where we use the notation that
\textnormal{XMDI}_{\{m\}}^{\dagger}=\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}^{\dagger}
and
\textnormal{XMDI}_{\{l,k\}}^{\dagger}=\textnormal{XMDI}_{lk}^{\dagger}
.

By (
A.80
)–(
A.81
) and the definition of XMDI
{}_{ij}^{\dagger}
’s, it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
,

\begin{split}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq M}|\textnormal{XMDI}_{ij}-\textnormal{XMDI}_{ij}^{\dagger}|&\leq\Delta+d_{n}+\widehat{\Gamma}.\end{split}

(A.82)

In addition, we observe that the estimation of additive effects remains consistent across both definitions of feature importance measures, due to the definition of
\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}
’s. Specifically, for each
1\leq m\leq M
,

\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}=\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}^{\dagger}.

(A.83)

Let us define some notation for further analysis:

\begin{split}\widehat{\Delta}_{\widehat{J}_{s}}&=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}\textnormal{ for each }0<s\leq K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*},\\
\widehat{\Delta}_{J}&=0\textnormal{ if }J\not\in\{\widehat{J}_{1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}\},\end{split}

where we recall that
R_{s}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})=R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})})
is defined in (
7
). Also, we use the notation
\widehat{\Delta}_{m}=\widehat{\Delta}_{\{m\}}
and
\widehat{\Delta}_{kl}=\widehat{\Delta}_{lk}=\widehat{\Delta}_{\{l,k\}}
for each
1\leq m\leq M
and every
1\leq l<k\leq M
.

By Lemma
3
, (
A.17
), and the assumed conditions in Theorem
2
, on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
, it holds that for each
0<l\leq K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}
,

\begin{split}|\textnormal{XMDI}_{\widehat{J}_{l}}^{\dagger}-\widehat{\Delta}_{\widehat{J}_{l}}|&\leq d_{n}.\end{split}

(A.84)

In addition, by the definitions of
\textnormal{XMDI}_{J}^{\dagger}
’s and
\widehat{\Delta}_{J}
’s, it holds that for every
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
such that
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
and
J\not\in\{\widehat{J}_{1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}\}
,

\textnormal{XMDI}_{J}^{\dagger}=\widehat{\Delta}_{J}=0.

(A.85)

By (
A.21
) and (
A.25
) and the assumed regularity conditions, it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
,

\begin{split}S_{1}^{\star}&\subset\cup_{1\leq l\leq K}\widehat{J}_{l},\\
S_{2}^{*}&\subset\{\widehat{J}_{K+1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}\}.\end{split}

By this sure screening result, the definition of significant components in
S_{1}^{*}
and
S_{2}^{*}
, (
A.85
), (
A.20
), and (
A.24
), it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
, for each
m\in\{1,\cdots,M\}
, each
\{l,k\}\in\{\widehat{J}_{K+1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}\}
, and each
\{i,j\}\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\{i,j\}\not\in\{\widehat{J}_{K+1},\cdots,\widehat{J}_{K+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}}\}
,

\begin{split}|\widehat{\Delta}_{m}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))|&\leq\frac{21\delta_{0}}{(p_{\min})^{2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}],\\
|\widehat{\Delta}_{lk}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{l}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X}))|&\leq 3808\delta_{0}{p_{\min}^{-2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}](\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{4},\\
|\widehat{\Delta}_{ij}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{ij}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{i}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{j}(\boldsymbol{X}))|&=0.\end{split}

(A.86)

Note that
\textnormal{Var}(g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
, implying
g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})=0
almost surely, for every
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
with
\texttt{\#}J=2
and
J\not\in S_{2}^{*}
.

By (
A.83
)–(
A.84
) and (
A.86
), it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
, for each
m\in\{1,\cdots,M\}
,

\begin{split}&|\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))|\\
&\leq|\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}-\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}^{\dagger}|+|\textnormal{XMDI}_{mm}^{\dagger}-\widehat{\Delta}_{m}|+|\widehat{\Delta}_{m}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{m}(\boldsymbol{X}))|\\
&\leq d_{n}+\frac{21\delta_{0}}{(p_{\min})^{2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}].\end{split}

(A.87)

By (
A.82
), (
A.84
), and (
A.86
), it holds that on the event
\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l}
, for each
l\in\{1,\cdots,M\}
,

\begin{split}&\sum_{k\not=l}|\textnormal{XMDI}_{lk}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{l}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X}))|\\
&\leq\sum_{k\not=l,1\leq k\leq M}\bigg(|\textnormal{XMDI}_{lk}-\textnormal{XMDI}_{lk}^{\dagger}|+|\textnormal{XMDI}_{lk}^{\dagger}-\widehat{\Delta}_{lk}|\\
&\qquad+|\widehat{\Delta}_{lk}-\textnormal{Var}(g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{l}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X}))|\bigg)\\
&\leq(\Delta+d_{n}+\widehat{\Gamma})+\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*}d_{n}+3808\delta_{0}{p_{\min}^{-2}}\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}](\texttt{\#}S_{2}^{*})^{5}.\end{split}

(A.88)

By (
A.87
)–(
A.88
), Lemma
5
, and the assumed regularity conditions, we conclude the desired results of Theorem
2
.

Appendix C
Auxiliary Lemmas and their proofs

C.1
Lemma
1
and its proof

Lemma 1
.

Assume that
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
. For every sequence of sets
J_{l}
’s, and functions
R_{l}
’s defined recursively such that
R_{0}(\boldsymbol{X})=0
and that for each
s>0
,

R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X})=R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J_{s})}),

it holds that

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X}))&=0,\\
\mathbb{E}|R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X})|&\leq 2\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}.\end{split}

(A.89)

Proof of Lemma
1
:
Since
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
, we deduce that

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X}))&=\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J_{s})}))\\
&=\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J_{s})}))+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))\\
&=\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}))-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}))\\
&=0\end{split}

for each
s>0
, which concludes the first assertion of Lemma
1
.

Next, we proceed to show the second assertion of Lemma
1
. By assumption, we deduce have that for each
s>0
,

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]\\
&=\mathbb{E}\{[f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J_{s})})]^{2}\}\\
&=\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]-\mathbb{E}\{[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J_{s})})]^{2}\}\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}],\end{split}

(A.90)

where the last inequality follows from a recursive application of the results before the last inequality, and the definition that
R_{0}(\boldsymbol{X})=0
.

By (
A.90
) and Jensen’s inequality,

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}|R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X})|&\leq\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s}(\boldsymbol{X})|+\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|\\
&\leq 2\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}.\end{split}

(A.91)

C.2
Lemma
2
and its proof

Lemma 2
.

For each
l>0
and set
J
with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
,

|\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})|\leq 3\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1}\qquad\textnormal{almost surely,}

(A.92)

where
p_{\min}>0
is defined in Condition
2
. Additionally, for each
s>0
,

\iota_{s}\leq s\times 3\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1},

(A.93)

where
\iota_{l}
’s are defined in (
8
).

Proof of Lemma
2
:

By the definition of
p_{\min}
in Condition
2
, it holds that

\min\{\mathbb{P}(\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}=\mathchoice{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern 2.0mu\displaystyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\displaystyle\mkern 0.0mu\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraita}$}}}\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\displaystyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern 2.0mu\textstyle\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraitd}$}}}\mkern-1.5mu\leaders{\hbox{$\textstyle\mkern 0.0mu\mathrel{\mathchoice{{}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\textstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\montraita}$}}{{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\montraita}$}}}\mkern 0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\textstyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern-0.7pt\cr$\mkern (A.94)

By the law of total expectation, we have that for every

with

,

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(|f(\boldsymbol{X})|)&=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}(|f(\boldsymbol{X})||\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})]\\

0.0mu$}}{\hfill}\mkern-1.5mu\fldr$\crcr\kern-0.3pt\cr$\hfil\scriptscriptstyle c\hfil$\crcr}}}).\end{split}

(A.95)

By (
A.94
)–(
A.95
) and Jensen’s inequality, for every
J\subset\{1,\cdots,p\}
with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
, it holds that almost surely

\mathbb{E}(|f(\boldsymbol{X})||\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})\leq(\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|)\times(p_{\min})^{-1}\leq\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1}.

By a similar calculation and the result of (
A.89
) from Lemma
1
, we have that for each
l\geq 0
and every set
J
with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
,

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(|R_{l}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})||\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})&\leq 2\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1}.\end{split}

(A.96)

Therefore, it holds that almost surely,

|\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{l-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})|\leq 3\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}\times p_{\min}^{-1}

for each
l>0
and every set
J
with
\texttt{\#}J\leq 2
, which in combination with the definition of
\iota_{s}
in (
8
) concludes the two desired results of Lemma
2
.

C.3
Lemma
3
and its proof

Lemma 3
.

For each
s>0
and every set
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
,

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}\\
&=\mathbb{E}[(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}))^{2}]\\
&=\textnormal{Var}[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})].\end{split}

(A.97)

Proof of Lemma
3
:

By the definitions of
R_{l}^{\star}
’s in (
7
) and
R_{s,J}^{\star}
in (
A.3
), the law of iterated expectation,

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s,J}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}\\
&=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}))^{2}\\
&=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}\\
&\qquad-2\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))\times\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})]\\
&\qquad+\mathbb{E}[(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}))^{2}]\\
&=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}-\mathbb{E}[(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}))^{2}].\end{split}

Lastly, since we have assumed
\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))=0
, and that

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}(R_{s}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))&=\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})}))\\
&=\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(\widehat{J}_{s})}))+\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X}))\\
&=\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))-\mathbb{E}(R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X}))\\
&=0\end{split}

for each
s>0
, we deduce that

\mathbb{E}[(\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)}))^{2}]=\textnormal{Var}[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-R_{s-1}^{\star}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(J)})],

which conclude the proof of Lemma
3
.

C.4
Lemma
4
and its proof

Lemma 4
.

For every
\{j,l,k\}\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
, it holds almost surely that

|\mathbb{E}\{g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{l}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\}|\leq\frac{8\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}},

where
g_{J}(\boldsymbol{X})
for each
J\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
is defined in Section
3
, and
p_{\min}
is defined in Condition
2
.

Proof of Lemma
4
:

Recall that
g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})
, and that
\mathcal{X}(jl)=\mathcal{X}(j)\cup\mathcal{X}(l)
. For every
\{j,l,k\}\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
, we deduce that

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}\{g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{l}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\}\\
&=\mathbb{E}\Big\{\mathbb{E}\left[f(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)}\right]\\
&\qquad-\mathbb{E}\left[f(\boldsymbol{X})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}\right]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\Big\}-\mathbb{E}\{g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\}\\
&=\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}\\
&\qquad+\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}]-\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}\\
&\qquad-\mathbb{E}\{g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\}.\end{split}

(A.98)

Let us deal with the first term on the RHS of (
A.98
). By Lemma
6
(where
j
corresponds to
l
in (
A.116
)) and Jensen’s inequality,

\begin{split}&|\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}-\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}\right\}|\\
&\leq\frac{2\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq\frac{2\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}.\end{split}

(A.99)

In addition, by the law of iterated expectation,

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}\right\}=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}),\\
&\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}=\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}).\end{split}

(A.100)

Hence, by (
A.99
)–(
A.100
),

\begin{split}&\left|\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})-\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}\right|\\
&=\bigg|\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}-\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}\right\}\\
&\qquad+\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}\right\}-\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}\bigg|\\
&\leq\frac{2\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}.\end{split}

(A.101)

Now, let us deal with the second term on the RHS of (
A.98
). By Lemma
6
and Jensen’s inequality,

\begin{split}\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)}\right\}&\leq\frac{3\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}},\\
\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}\right\}&\leq\frac{\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}},\end{split}

implying that almost surely

\begin{split}&\mathbb{E}\left\{\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)}]-\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}(f(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(lk)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lk)}]|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\right\}\\
&\leq\frac{4\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}.\end{split}

(A.102)

For the third term on the RHS of (
A.98
), by Lemma
6
and (
A.53
), we deduce that

|\mathbb{E}\{g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\}|\leq\frac{\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}\leq\frac{2\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}.

(A.103)

By (
A.98
), (
A.101
)–(
A.103
), and Jensen’s inequality, it holds almost surely that

\begin{split}&\left|\mathbb{E}\{g_{lk}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{l}(\boldsymbol{X})-g_{k}(\boldsymbol{X})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(lj)}\}\right|\\
&\leq\frac{2\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}+\frac{4\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|f(\boldsymbol{X})|}{p_{\min}}+\frac{2\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}\\
&\leq\frac{8\delta_{0}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(f(\boldsymbol{X}))^{2}]}}{p_{\min}}.\end{split}

(A.104)

C.5
Lemma
5
and its proof

Let
E_{41},\cdots,E_{46}
be defined as in (
A.10
).

Lemma 5
.

Assume Condition
1
, that
(\boldsymbol{X}_{1},Y_{1}),\cdots,(\boldsymbol{X}_{n},Y_{n}),(\boldsymbol{X},Y)
are i.i.d., and that
\mathbb{E}(\varepsilon\times\boldsymbol{1}\{|\varepsilon|\leq n^{\frac{1}{q_{1}}}\}|\boldsymbol{X})=0
for each
n>0
, in which
q_{1}
is an arbitrary constant with
q_{0}>q_{1}>0
.
Assume
M=O(n^{K_{01}})
for an arbitrary constant
K_{01}>0
,
t_{1}=t_{2}=\log{(n)}n^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{q_{1}}}
,
t_{3}=t_{4}=t_{6}=\log{(n)}\sqrt{n}
, and
t_{5}=2n\mathbb{E}\varepsilon^{2}
. Then, it holds that
\mathbb{P}((\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l})^{c})=o(1)
, where
A^{c}
denotes the complementary event of event
A
.

Proof of Lemma
5
:

Define
\epsilon_{i}=\varepsilon_{i}\times\boldsymbol{1}\{|\varepsilon_{i}|\leq n^{\frac{1}{q_{1}}}\}
, and that
E_{4}=\cap_{i=1}^{n}\{\epsilon_{i}=\varepsilon_{i}\}
. By assumption,

\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{i}|\boldsymbol{X}_{i})=0,

(A.105)

and that

\begin{split}\mathbb{P}(\cup_{i=1}^{n}\{\epsilon_{i}\not=\varepsilon_{i}\})&\leq\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{P}(|\varepsilon_{i}|\geq n^{\frac{1}{q_{1}}})\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{P}(|\varepsilon_{i}|^{q_{0}}\geq n^{\frac{q_{0}}{q_{1}}})\\
&\leq n^{1-\frac{q_{0}}{q_{1}}}\times\mathbb{E}|\varepsilon|^{q_{0}}.\end{split}

(A.106)

The above results of (
A.105
) and (
A.106
) are required for establishing the upper bound of
\mathbb{P}((\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l})^{c})
as follows. Let us deduce that

\begin{split}&\mathbb{P}((\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l})^{c})\\
&\leq\mathbb{P}(E_{4}^{c})+\mathbb{P}(E_{4}\cap(\cap_{l=1}^{6}E_{4l})^{c})\\
&\leq\mathbb{P}(E_{4}^{c})+\mathbb{P}\left(\left\{\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\epsilon_{i}f(\boldsymbol{X}_{i})\right|>t_{1}\right\}\right)\\

(A.111)

Let us move on to the next probability upper bound. By Hoeffding’s inequality, that
-n^{2q_{1}^{-1}}\leq\epsilon_{i}^{2}-\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{i})^{2}\leq n^{2q_{1}^{-1}}
, it holds that for each
t_{5}>0
,

\begin{split}&\mathbb{P}\left(\left\{\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\epsilon_{i}^{2}-\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{1}^{2})+\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{1}^{2}))\right|>t_{5}\right\}\right)\\
&\leq\mathbb{P}\left(\left\{\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\epsilon_{i}^{2}-\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{1}^{2})\right|>t_{5}-n\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{1}^{2}))\right\}\right)\\
&\leq\exp\left(\frac{-2(t_{5}-n\mathbb{E}(\epsilon_{1}^{2}))^{2}}{4n^{1+4q_{1}^{-1}}}\right).\end{split}

(A.112)

In addition, simple calculations show that

\mathbb{E}\epsilon_{1}^{2}=\mathbb{E}\left[\varepsilon_{1}^{2}\boldsymbol{1}\{|\varepsilon_{1}|\leq n^{q_{1}^{-1}}\}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}\varepsilon_{1}^{2}=\mathbb{E}\varepsilon^{2}.

(A.113)

&\leq\delta_{0}\times\frac{\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|}{\mathbb{P}(X_{l}=1)}.\end{split}

(A.120)

By similar arguments for (
A.120
), it holds almost surely that for each measurable
q:\mathbb{R}^{p-\texttt{\#}\mathcal{X}(m)}\mapsto\mathbb{R}
and
\texttt{\#}\mathcal{X}(m)>1
,

|\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}))-\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})|\leq\delta_{0}\times\frac{\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|}{\min_{l\in\mathcal{X}(m)}\mathbb{P}(X_{l}=1)}.

(A.121)

By similar arguments, it holds almost surely that for
\texttt{\#}\mathcal{X}(m)=1
,

|\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}))-\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})|\leq\delta_{0}\times\frac{\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|}{\mathbb{P}(X_{l}=1)\wedge\mathbb{P}(X_{l}=0)}.

Therefore, we deduce almost surely that for each
m\in\{1,\cdots,M\}
,

|\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)}))-\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(m)})|\leq\delta_{0}\times\frac{\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(m)})|}{\min_{1\leq m\leq M,l\in\mathcal{X}(m),a\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb{P}(X_{l}=a)},

which concludes the proof of the first assertion of Lemma
6
.

(A.123)

which, in conjunction with the definition of
p_{\min}
in Condition
2
, implies almost surely that for every
\{l,k\}\subset\{1,\cdots,M\}
,

\begin{split}&|\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(k)},\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)})-\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(k)})|\\
&\leq\max_{\ i\in\mathcal{X}(k),j\in\mathcal{X}(l),(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^{2}}\frac{2\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|}{\mathbb{P}(X_{i}=a,X_{j}=b)}\\
&\leq\frac{2\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(l)})|}{p_{\min}}.\end{split}

This result concludes the proof of the second assertion of Lemma
6
.

(A.124)

A.124
), we derive that for every
1\leq k<l\leq M
, it holds that almost surely,

\begin{split}&|\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(kl)})|\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(k)},\boldsymbol{X}_{\mathcal{X}(l)})-\mathbb{E}(q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(kl)}))|\\
&\leq\max_{\ i\in\mathcal{X}(k),j\in\mathcal{X}(l),(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^{2}}\frac{3\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(kl)})|}{\mathbb{P}(X_{i}=a,X_{j}=b)}\\
&\leq\frac{3\delta_{0}\mathbb{E}|q(\boldsymbol{X}_{-\mathcal{X}(kl)})|}{p_{\min}},\end{split}

which concludes the proof of the third assertion of Lemma
6
, and hence finishes the proof of Lemma
6
.
